significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: subliminally laden data produce an "anomalously consistent" low-dimensional gradient fingerprint, while specified surface transformations reduce trait transfer more than benign utility. This establishes both a phenomenon—a detectable concentration/transfer relationship—and a partial mechanism locating the channel in "specific non-semantic surface tokens," thereby fixing expectations for unseen traits and transformation choices rather than merely identifying one causal steering direction. Cloud et al., "Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data" (2025), reports semantically unrelated trait transfer and matched-base-model dependence, so a false result would still meaningfully rule out a generic gradient-fingerprint audit and cheap surface-channel account, although the words "anomalously" and "favorable trade-off" leave thresholds somewhat underdetermined. Topic-substitution check: merely restating the assignment to extend subliminal learning would not earn this score; the trait-agnostic predictive coupling and selective transformation law are the claim-specific increments.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Subliminal Gradient Audit (SGA)" and the proposed "surface-form-preserving transformations," respectively an ex-ante screen of a candidate dataset before student training and a preventive data-processing design rule. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed relation still predicts that laden examples will concentrate along a small latent subspace, so it transfers as a predictive coupling rather than only as a procedure for searching; however, the claim concedes that it may cover only "steering-vector-style biases." Its asserted scope includes unknown traits and Qwen, Llama, and Gemma settings, with downstream uptake by practitioners who audit or gate distillation datasets before training, rather than solely by researchers explaining completed failures. Topic-substitution check: the topic alone supplies neither this pre-training handle nor its action window, so the score rests on claim-specific reach, though the limited mechanism coverage prevents a 9–10.
